title: Revolutionary Worth: Reclaiming Inherent Worth and Mattering for Collective Liberation
abstract: Revolutionary Worth traces the Worth Wound —the inherited consequences of societies that organize human value into hierarchy—from colonial violence and racialization to contemporary expressions in perfectionism, toxic productivity, achievement culture, and comparison. Drawing from liberation psychology, critical race scholarship, Indigenous and ancestral wisdom, and mattering science, this address examines how systems of domination become internalized as conditions of worth. It distinguishes inherent worth, an embodied knowing of significance that cannot be earned or revoked, from mattering, the relational experience of being valued and contributing value to others. Together, these constructs offer a framework for understanding human hierarchy and a pathway to liberation. The address proposes that psychology ought to move beyond symptom reduction and individual resilience toward an ecology of care in which individual healing catalyzes change across families, communities, organizations, and institutions organized around inherent worth and relational mattering.
